value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the task requires reaching the goal after opening the door, but the only clause makes the agent acquire the key first. Add a clause that makes the agent open the door after acquiring the key, and a clause that makes the agent reach the goal after opening the door.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task requires the agent to acquire the key first, but the only Existence clause is for the key. Add a hard Existence for the key acquisition step. The machine will then reward the agent for acquiring the key and will still reward the agent for reaching the goal. The task also requires the agent to reach the goal, so an Existence clause for the goal is also required. The machine will then reward the agent for reaching the goal. The final state of the machine will be u1 when the agent has acquired the key and reached the goal. The machine does not have a rejecting state because there are no hard rules that can be broken for good. The task requires the agent to acquire the key first, then reach the goal. The compiled machine is correct for the clauses it received. The only thing that can be wrong is the set of clauses: whether it captures the task.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The task commands 'Grab the key first, then make your way to the goal', but the only clause is 'Grab the key first', which only requires acquiring the key, not reaching the goal. Add a clause that requires reaching the goal after acquiring the key. The task also implies that 'make your way to the goal' requires 'open the door after acquiring the key', which is not captured. Keep the 'Grab the key first' clause but add a new clause to require reaching the goal after acquiring the key.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task requires reaching the goal after grabbing the key, but the hard Existence(has_key) only requires grabbing the key. Add a hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal) to require the goal after the key; keep the hard Existence(has_key) and no other hard order clause. The hard Precedence alone is wrong, because 'Grab the key first' does not turn the requirement into a restriction: the task commands grabbing the key, so it must happen.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task is not only to acquire the key (the hard Existence), but to do so first (the phrase "Grab the key first"); the machine rewards only acquiring the key on its first step. The task also commands to make your way to the goal after acquiring the key, which requires the agent to open the door (no rule for it). The candidate is incomplete and contains no rule for opening the door, so add the Precedence(has_key, door_open) rule; it requires the key to be acquired first and the door to be open before the goal is reached.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task is to grab the key first, then make your way to the goal, but no clause makes the key first happen. Add a hard Existence(key_lost) and keep the hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal). Existence(key_lost) is owed when the key is dropped and never carried again, which makes the agent first grab the key. The existing hard Existence(has_key) only makes the key happen, not before the goal. The episode ends when the agent reaches the goal, so has_key needs to happen before at_goal. The existing hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal) already forces the goal to happen after the key is acquired, but it does not make the key first happen.

NO CHANGES NEEDED: the candidate correctly captures the task. Existence(has_key) makes the key happen, Precedence(has_key, door_open) puts acquiring the key before opening the door, and Precedence(door_open, at_goal) keeps the order. The machine has a final state u1, which only requires has_key and door_open, and there is no missing Existence or order. The warning is rule-only, which is correct because the task does not require the agent to reach the goal unconditionally. The agent does this as a result of the Precedence chain.
